title: "TERRE GRS: Prediction of case-control status"

The manuscript "A Parkinson’s disease genetic risk score associates with blood DNAm on chromosome 17" explores how a genetic risk score (GRS) for Parkinson's disease (PD) associates with blood DNA methylation in the TERRE study of French agricultural workers, and evaluates GRS associations with DNAm in each sex as well as their sensitivity to non-genetic factors. This was originally spearheaded by Will Casazza and was posted as a pre-print on medRxiv in 2023. The current revision (2024, led by Sam Schaffner) aims to address previous reviewer feedback and prepare the manuscript for re-submission.


This script evaluates how well the GRS can predict case-control status, in a cross-sex sample and sex-stratified samples. 


Last updated Mar 8, 2026 by Samantha Schaffner: Adding 95% CI.

Based on code by Will Casazza

# PD risk score data and matching

### Loading in and preparing data

This code reads in the Nalls 2019 PD risk score loci and organizes it into a table with alleles and weights for each SNP. Here, I matched the meta data with the CMR project meta data that includes cell type PCs and batch information.
```{r risk score dat, eval=FALSE}
risk_scores <- read.delim("~/PD_GRS/WC_scripts/prs_analyses/gp2_2025_prs_file.txt", header=FALSE, sep=" ")
head(risk_scores) #157 GP2 SNPs and their weights
#          V1 V2      V3
#1   rs377808  G -0.0486
#2 rs12128848  G -0.0414
#3 rs76763715  C  0.8378
#4 rs75548401  A  0.3649
#5  rs2230288  T  0.4595
#6 rs72712862  T  0.2103

digpd_prs <- fread("~/PD_GRS/WC_scripts/prs_analyses/digpd_prs_gp2_2025.sscore")
# GRS computed in DIGPD based on 119/157 SNPs present after QC filtering

# DNAm data
load("~/SHARE_DECIPHER/processed_DNAm_data/2022/DIGPD_processed_2022/1-DIGPD_RG_filtered.RData")
mvals <- getM(DIGPD_RG_filtered)
```

# Testing how well GRS explains case-control status

GRS performance is assessed here by comparing models predicting case-control status that include or do not include the GRS. The nagelkerke() function from the "rcompanion" package produces pseudo R-squared measurements, which indicate how well each model explains the data relative to each other. A higher R squared indicates better prediction of the outcome. The Nagelkerke measure is an more interpretable adjustment of the Cox and Snell measure, where the upper bound is 1.

Liability scale heritability for the PD GRS is also calculated, which assumes there is a continuous distribution of risk for PD that is influenced by genetic and environmental factors. Heritability is interpreted here as the proportion of variance in PD risk that is due to genetics.

### Scale GRS
The GRS should have a mean of 0 and SD of 1 after scaling.
```{r scale, eval=F}
meta <- read.csv("~/PD_GRS/digpd_meta_geno_DNAm_PCs_22Feb26.csv")

# check scaling of PGS: should have mean of 0, SD of 1
mean(meta$SCORE1_AVG) #0.002095215
sd(meta$SCORE1_AVG) #0.001659124
plot(density(meta$SCORE1_AVG))

meta$GRS_scaled <- scale(meta$SCORE1_AVG)
mean(meta$GRS_scaled) #6.331741e-17
sd(meta$GRS_scaled) #1

#mean and SD by PD status
meta_PD <- meta[meta$PD==1,]
mean(meta_PD$GRS_scaled) #0.2018398
sd(meta_PD$GRS_scaled) #1.000298

meta_ctrl <- meta[meta$PD==0,]
mean(meta_ctrl$GRS_scaled) #-0.1982356
sd(meta_ctrl$GRS_scaled) #0.9635347

par(mfrow=c(2,1))
plot(density(meta$SCORE1_AVG), main="GRS prior to scaling", xlim=c(-3,3))
plot(density(meta$GRS_scaled), main="GRS after scaling", xlim=c(-3,3))

write.csv(meta, file="~/PD_GRS/digpd_meta_geno_DNAm_PCs_22Feb26.csv", row.names=F) 
```

## Model with genotype PCs only
```{r model genoPCs, eval=F}
fit1 <- glm(PD ~ GRS_scaled + reportedSex + Age + GPC1 + GPC2 + GPC3, data = meta, family = "binomial")
summary(fit1) #GRS: p = 0.00248
fit1_null <- glm(PD ~ reportedSex + Age + GPC1 + GPC2 + GPC3, data = meta, family = "binomial")
summary(fit1_null) #nothing sig
(cross_r2 <- nagelkerke(fit1, null = fit1_null))
#                             Pseudo.R.squared
#McFadden                            0.0317087
#Cox and Snell (ML)                  0.0428647
#Nagelkerke (Cragg and Uhler)        0.0572417

#bootstrapping to generate 95% CI for R squared
library(boot)
library(rcompanion)

get_nagelkerke <- function(data, indices) {
  boot_data <- data[indices, ]
  fit1 <- glm(PD ~ GRS_scaled + reportedSex + Age + GPC1 + GPC2 + GPC3, boot_data, family = "binomial")
  fit1_null <- glm(PD ~ reportedSex + Age + GPC1 + GPC2 + GPC3, boot_data, family = "binomial")
  r2_out <- suppressWarnings(nagelkerke(fit1, null=fit1_null))
  nagelkerke_val <- as.numeric(r2_out$Pseudo.R.squared.for.model.vs.null[3])
  return(nagelkerke_val)
}

set.seed(123)
boot_results <- boot(data = meta, statistic = get_nagelkerke, R = 1000, strata = as.factor(meta$PD))
boot.ci(boot_results, type = "bca")
#Level       BCa          
#95%   ( 0.0060,  0.1527 )  

#liability scale heritability calculation, mirroring Lee et al. approach
lee_h2 <- function(R2O, case_prop, prevalence) {
  K <- prevalence
  P <- case_prop
  thd <- qnorm(1 - K) # Threshold
  z <- dnorm(thd) # Height of the normal density at the threshold
  h2_liab <- R2O * (K * (1 - K) / z^2) * (K * (1 - K) / (P * (1 - P)))
  return(h2_liab)
}

R2 <- cross_r2$Pseudo.R.squared.for.model.vs.null[3]
summary(as.factor(meta$PD))
#  0   1 
#112 110 
h2 <- lee_h2(R2, 110/222, 5/1000)
R2 #0.0572417
h2 #0.02710646
```

## Sex-stratified models
```{r sex strat r2, eval=F}
fit1_male <- glm(PD ~ GRS_scaled + Age + GPC1 + GPC2 + GPC3, data = meta[meta$reportedSex == "M", ], family = "binomial")
summary(fit1_male) #GRS scaled: p = 0.00348
fit1_male_null <- glm(PD ~ Age + GPC1 + GPC2 + GPC3, data = meta[meta$reportedSex == "M", ], family = "binomial")
summary(fit1_male_null) #nothing significant
(male_r2 <- nagelkerke(fit1_male, null = fit1_male_null))
#                             Pseudo.R.squared
#McFadden                            0.0532174
#Cox and Snell (ML)                  0.0697910
#Nagelkerke (Cragg and Uhler)        0.0939066

get_nagelkerke_strat <- function(data, indices) {
  boot_data <- data[indices, ]
  fit1 <- glm(PD ~ GRS_scaled + Age + GPC1 + GPC2 + GPC3, boot_data, family = "binomial")
  fit1_null <- glm(PD ~ Age + GPC1 + GPC2 + GPC3, boot_data, family = "binomial")
  r2_out <- suppressWarnings(nagelkerke(fit1, null=fit1_null))
  nagelkerke_val <- as.numeric(r2_out$Pseudo.R.squared.for.model.vs.null[3])
  return(nagelkerke_val)
}

boot_results <- boot(data = meta[meta$reportedSex == "M", ], statistic = get_nagelkerke_strat, R = 1000, strata = as.factor(meta[meta$reportedSex == "M", "PD"]))
boot.ci(boot_results, type = "bca")
#Level       BCa          
#95%   ( 0.0127,  0.2306 ) 

# liability R2 for updated male model
R2 <- male_r2$Pseudo.R.squared.for.model.vs.null[3]
summary(as.factor(meta[meta$reportedSex%in%"M","PD"]))
# 0  1 
#66 63 
h2 <- lee_h2(R2, 63/129, 5/1000)
R2 #0.0939066
h2 #0.04448935

fit1_female <- glm(PD ~ GRS_scaled + Age + GPC1 + GPC2 + GPC3, data = meta[meta$reportedSex == "F", ], family = "binomial")
summary(fit1_female) #GRS p = 0.183
fit1_female_null <- glm(PD ~  Age + GPC1 + GPC2 + GPC3, data = meta[meta$reportedSex == "F", ], family = "binomial")
summary(fit1_female_null) #nothing sig
(female_r2 <- nagelkerke(fit1_female, null = fit1_female_null))
#                             Pseudo.R.squared
#McFadden                            0.0146508
#Cox and Snell (ML)                  0.0195059
#Nagelkerke (Cragg and Uhler)        0.0263828

boot_results <- boot(data = meta[meta$reportedSex == "F", ], statistic = get_nagelkerke_strat, R = 1000, strata = as.factor(meta[meta$reportedSex == "F", "PD"]))
boot.ci(boot_results, type = "bca")
#Level       BCa          
#95%   ( 0.0001,  0.1528 )  

# liability R2 for updated female model
R2 <- female_r2$Pseudo.R.squared.for.model.vs.null[3]
summary(as.factor(meta[meta$reportedSex=="F","PD"]))
# 0  1 
#46 47 
h2 <- lee_h2(R2, 93/100, 5/1000)
R2 #0.0263828
h2 #0.04797389
```

### Plotting cross-sex and sex-stratified GRS models
```{r plot GRS, eval=F}
r2_labels <- c(0.0572,0.0939,0.0264)
names(r2_labels) <- c("Cross-sex","Male","Female")

pval_labels <- c(
  round(cross_r2$Likelihood.ratio.test[4], 4),
  round(male_r2$Likelihood.ratio.test[4], 4),
  round(female_r2$Likelihood.ratio.test[4], 4)
)
names(pval_labels) <- c("Cross-sex", "Male", "Female")

to_plot <- meta %>%
  mutate(
    PD = ifelse(PD, "CASE", "CONTROL"),
    Sex = ifelse(reportedSex == "M", "Male", "Female")
  ) %>%  mutate(Sex = factor(Sex, levels = c("Cross-sex", "Male", "Female")))
cross_data <- meta %>% mutate(PD = ifelse(PD, "CASE", "CONTROL"))
cross_data$Sex <- "Cross-sex"
to_plot <- rbind(cross_data, to_plot)
library(DescTools)
to_plot$Sex <- as.factor(to_plot$Sex)
to_plot$Sex <- reorder.factor(to_plot$Sex, new.order=c("Cross-sex","Male","Female"))
to_plot$PD <- as.factor(to_plot$PD)
to_plot$PD <- reorder.factor(to_plot$PD, new.order=c("CONTROL","CASE"))

png("~/PD_GRS/DIGPD_prs_plots_by_PD_sex_8Mar2026.png", width=600, height=500)
ggboxplot(
  to_plot,
  x = "PD",
  y = "GRS_scaled",
  color = "Sex",
  add = "jitter"
) +
  facet_grid(~Sex, labeller = label_bquote(cols = .(as.character(Sex)) ~ R^2 ~ ": " ~ .(r2_labels[Sex]) ~ ";" ~ p-value ~ ": " ~ .(pval_labels[Sex]))) +
  labs(y = "Genetic Risk Score (Scaled)", x = "Parkinson's Diagnosis") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("gray", "lightblue", "pink")) + stat_compare_means(method="t.test", label.x.npc="center",hjust=0.5)
dev.off()

png("~/PD_GRS/DIGPD_prs_plots_by_sex_1Mar2026.png", width=300, height=500)
ggboxplot(
  to_plot,
  x = "Sex",
  y = "GRS_scaled",
  color = "Sex",
  add = "jitter"
) +
  stat_compare_means() +

  labs(y = "Genetic Risk Score (Scaled)") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Male" = "light blue", "Female" = "pink"))
dev.off()
```
